Both! The illustrations on the left are the view of the turbine from the front, and the illustrations on the right are a cross-section of the intake.

When a jet is flying at super sonic speeds, it has to reposition the point of air intake. This is because the shock wave thsts constantly being created by the leading edges of the aircraft disrupt the air flow.

Also the super sonic speeds kind of shove more air into the engine sort of like a ramjet. This is why the shutters close, I imagine it also helps with the thinner air of higher altitude by pressuring the air further.

Most importantly though it's to negate the turbulence of the supersonic shock wave by moving where the sonic boom breaks.

You also need to slow the super sonic air down to subsonic speeds so that it's usable for the engine.
